data.description:
## Description

**What**: Update `/dso:onboarding` to write `dso.workflow=ci-pr` or `dso.workflow=local` to `dso-config.conf` based on GitHub remote detection, instead of writing the four legacy keys.

**Why**: New host projects must start on the canonical config key from day one. Onboarding is the write path for first-time setup; ensuring it produces `dso.workflow` means migrated and new projects converge on the same config format.

**Scope**:
- IN: Update the onboarding skill to write `dso.workflow` instead of legacy keys; GitHub remote detection logic (https/ssh → `ci-pr`, everything else → `local`); fixture shell tests for four remote types; round-trip test (onboarding → migrator → assert no-op on second migrator run)
- OUT: The migrator (S2), read-config.sh changes (S1), hot-path script changes (S5)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `/dso:onboarding` on a project whose `git remote get-url origin` matches `https://github.com/` or `git@github.com:` writes `dso.workflow=ci-pr` to `dso-config.conf`
  ← Satisfies: SC4 (GitHub remote → ci-pr)
- When this story is complete, `/dso:onboarding` on a project with no origin, a GitLab remote, or an enterprise GitHub host writes `dso.workflow=local` to `dso-config.conf`
  ← Satisfies: SC4 (non-GitHub remotes → local)
- When this story is complete, `read-config.sh` when invoked against a missing `dso-config.conf` directs the user to run `/dso:onboarding` (non-zero exit with message)
  ← Satisfies: SC4 (read-config.sh directs to onboarding)
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Enterprise GitHub hosts (not `github.com`) must default to `local` pending explicit user override — the detection logic must not match enterprise URLs
- [Conflicting Assumptions] The `dso-config.conf` written by `/dso:onboarding` must use the grammar the migrator accepts as already-migrated: bare `dso.workflow=<value>` with LF line endings, no inline comments on the value line, no quotes. Add a round-trip test: run `/dso:onboarding` on a fresh fixture → run migrator → assert second migrator run is a no-op (idempotency holds across onboarding+migrator boundary).

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a new host project, /dso:onboarding writes dso.workflow based on GitHub remote detection
